history.dynasty: Local community stewardship; present temple associated with Sakthan Thampuran era (late 18th c.)
history.period: About 400 years old per tradition (UNVERIFIED by dated inscription)
history.summary: Thiruvambadi Sri Krishna Temple, near Punkunnam in Thrissur, enshrines Krishna as Unnikrishna (infant Krishna), with Bhagavathy (Balabhadrakali) at his left. Tradition says the community moved here about four centuries ago with their moola vigrahas to escape communal violence; the idols were entrusted to a childless Namboodiri couple of Kachanappilly Illam, who worshipped Parthasarathy as their own child, then handed the temple to the public. It is one of the two rival temple groups of the Thrissur Pooram (Thiruvambadi side vs Paramekkavu side), the festival having been choreographed by Sakthan Thampuran (Rama Varma, 1751-1805). The Pooram ceremonially begins with the Madathil Varavu procession from this temple.

name: Thiruvambadi Sri Krishna Temple
town_description: Thrissur is a major city in central Kerala, often called the cultural capital of the state for its temples, pooram festivals and classical arts. Thiruvambadi temple lies on Shornur Road near Punkunnam, about 1 km from the Vadakkunnathan Temple at the city centre. Thrissur is a key rail junction linking north and south Kerala.
